Exercise A

How Advertisements Work

Read the text about advertising. Fill in each gap with the correct word.

Reading Text

Advertisements are everywhere. Companies spend billions of dollars every year to 1 us to buy their products. A good advertisement grabs your 2 immediately, often with bright colours or a catchy 3.

Many adverts use famous people, or 4, because we tend to trust the products they recommend. Others make special 5, such as "buy one, get one free", to make us feel we are saving money.

Advertisers also know that words are powerful. Phrases like "brand 6" or "limited 7" make a product sound exciting and rare. Some adverts even make us feel that we 8 something we never wanted before. The next time you see an advert, ask yourself: is this information, or is someone trying to change my mind?

Exercise B

Persuasive Language in Slogans

Advertisers use commands (imperatives) and strong adjectives to persuade us. Complete each slogan with the correct word.

Complete the Slogan
Watch for: Discover best miss Try amazing limited free new

1. " our brand new range today!"

2. "The pizza in town!"

3. "Don't this incredible deal!"

4. " it now — you will love it!"

Exercise C

Writing: Your Own Advertisement

Invent a product and write an advertisement for it (6–8 sentences). Use at least three persuasive words from this lesson.

Useful persuasive words
You can use these: discover the best don't miss try it now amazing brand new limited offer free special incredible
Your advertisement
Aim for 6–8 sentences. Use at least 3 persuasive words.
